newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares rise in heaviest trade this year.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares rise in heaviest trade this year.

text.p: Shares on the Amman stock exchange rose on Tuesday in the busiest trading this year, shrugging off losses in heavyweight Arab Bank to rise 0.18 percent.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.27 points to 153.51 points in business worth 3.57 million dinars ($5.04 million).
Brokers said the volume and prices were boosted by end of year portfolio adjustments and by continued optimism that Jordanian firms would benefit from Iraq's oil-for-food deal.

"Some of the big investors are trying to drive up their investments because their portfolios will be re-evaluated at the end of the year," said Nasser al-Amad, general manager of United Financial Investments.

Transport firm Unified Company and National Industrial, both expected to benefit from the limited resumption of Iraqi oil exports, rose 0.07 dinars to 2.21 dinars and 0.03 dinars to 0.71 dinars respectively in busy turnover.
Jordan Phosphates and Minerals also rose 0.05 dinars to 3.30 dinars, helping to offset a 1.50 dinar fall in Arab Bank shares to 253.50 dinars. Arab Bank turnover was worth over two million dinars.
Brokers say Arab Bank, a safe haven share during the frequent bouts of political anxiety which plague the Amman bourse, often slips when other shares are bouncing up.
"When nothing else looks good, people buy into Arab Bank, so it's bound to slide if they're taking their money out and investing in the other shares," said Nasser.
Another gainer was International Tobacco, which rose 0.06 dinars to 1.31 dinars in trade worth 155,000 dinars.
"This company is expected to make a 1996 net profit of 1.5 million dinars -- that's 15 percent of paid up capital," Amad said. "And people are looking ahead to a stronger performance in 1997."
Overall 33 shares rose on Tuesday. Five fell and six traded but closed unchanged.
